items.q: End diastolic volume is 120 ml and end systolic volume is 50 ml by Simpson biplane. What is the ejection fraction?
items.exp: Ejection fraction equals stroke volume over end diastolic volume, so 70 over 120 reads about 58 percent. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left ventricular ejection fraction.

items.q: Which two planes make the Simpson biplane ejection fraction?
o: Apical four chamber and apical two chamber
items.exp: Two perpendicular apical planes trace the cavity without geometry guesses, so four chamber with two chamber is the pair. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left ventricular volumes.

items.q: When tracing Simpson volumes, where is the endocardial border placed?
o: Through the middle of the papillary muscles
At the compacted wall excluding trabeculations from the cavity
items.exp: The cavity holds the blood pool, so the trace follows compacted muscle and keeps papillary tissue out of the volume. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on border tracing.

items.q: A foreshortened apical view is used for Simpson volumes. What error follows?
o: Volumes read small and ejection fraction may mislead
items.exp: A cut apex shortens the long axis, so both volumes fall and decisions based on them shift wrongly. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on avoiding foreshortening.

items.q: Left atrial volume index is 38 ml per sq m. How is the atrium graded?
items.exp: Indexing to body surface with 34 ml per sq m as the upper limit makes 38 dilated rather than normal. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left atrial volume.

items.q: How is left atrial volume best measured?
o: Biplane area length from four and two chamber at end systole
items.exp: Two perpendicular areas at maximal atrial size avoid single plane error, so biplane area length indexed to surface is standard. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left atrial volume.

items.q: TAPSE is 14 mm. How is right ventricular function graded?
items.exp: Annular excursion below 17 mm means weak longitudinal shortening, so systolic function reads reduced. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on TAPSE.

items.q: Where is TAPSE measured?
o: M mode at the lateral tricuspid annulus in the four chamber view
items.exp: Longitudinal right ventricular motion shows at the lateral tricuspid ring, so M mode there gives TAPSE directly. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on TAPSE.

items.q: TR peak velocity is 2.9 m per s with normal veins. What does it suggest?
o: Raised pulmonary pressure needing full assessment
items.exp: Velocity above 2.8 m per s lifts the estimated systolic pressure, so pulmonary hypertension enters the differential. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2016 diastolic function guideline, section on tricuspid velocity in filling pressure assessment.

items.q: TR peak velocity is 3.0 m per s and right atrial pressure is estimated at 10 mmHg. What is PASP?
items.exp: Bernoulli gives 4 times 9 equals 36, and adding atrial pressure 10 gives about 46 mmHg systolic. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on pulmonary pressure estimation.

items.q: Average E over e prime is 17. What does it mean?
items.exp: Average E over e prime above 14 tracks high left atrial pressure, so 17 reads raised rather than normal. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2016 diastolic function guideline, section on E over e prime.

items.q: Septal e prime is 5 cm per s and lateral e prime is 7 cm per s. How is relaxation graded?
items.exp: Cutoffs near 7 septal and 10 lateral mark normal annular motion, so values below both mean impaired relaxation. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2016 diastolic function guideline, section on annular velocities.

items.q: Mitral E over A is 0.6 with a slow E fall. What pattern is this?
items.exp: E below A with slow deceleration marks slow early filling, which is the grade one relaxation pattern. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2016 diastolic function guideline, section on mitral inflow patterns.

items.q: Mitral E over A is 2.5 with a short deceleration. What pattern is this?
items.exp: Tall E with rapid fall marks high pressure stiff filling, which fits restriction rather than slow relaxation. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2016 diastolic function guideline, section on mitral inflow patterns.

items.q: Peak aortic velocity is 4.2 m per s with mean gradient 45 mmHg and area 0.9 sq cm. What grade is this?
items.exp: Velocity above 4 with mean gradient above 40 and area below 1.0 meets all three severe bands together. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on aortic stenosis severity.

items.q: Peak aortic velocity is 2.5 m per s with mean gradient 18 mmHg and area 1.8 sq cm. What grade is this?
items.exp: Velocity below 3 with gradient below 20 and area above 1.5 sits in the mild band on all three measures. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on aortic stenosis severity.

items.q: In the continuity equation, what does the LVOT provide?
o: The reference stroke volume from diameter and VTI
items.exp: Flow through one known area equals flow through the stenotic valve, so LVOT size with its VTI anchors the equation. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on continuity equation.

items.q: Where is the LVOT diameter measured?
o: Parasternal long axis at the valve base in mid systole
Apical four chamber at the apex
items.exp: The outflow width is best seen in the long axis cut at the base, and small errors here square up in area. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on outflow measurement.

items.q: LVOT diameter is 2.0 cm with VTI 20 cm. What is the stroke volume?
items.exp: Area equals 3.14 times radius squared, so 3.14 sq cm times 20 cm gives about 63 ml per beat. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on stroke volume by Doppler.

items.q: Mitral valve area is 0.8 sq cm with mean gradient 12 mmHg. What grade is this?
items.exp: Area below 1.0 with gradient above 10 marks severe obstruction with left atrial pressure load. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on mitral stenosis severity.

items.q: Mitral valve area is 1.2 sq cm with mean gradient 7 mmHg. What grade is this?
items.exp: Area between 1.0 and 1.5 with gradient 5 to 10 sits in the moderate band. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on mitral stenosis severity.

items.q: Pressure half time is 300 ms across a stenotic mitral valve. What area does 220 over PHT give?
items.exp: 220 divided by 300 gives about 0.7, which lies below 1.0 and reads severe with slow pressure fall. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on pressure half time.

items.q: EROA is 0.45 sq cm with regurgitant volume 65 ml for mitral regurgitation. What grade is this?
items.exp: Orifice at or above 0.40 with volume at or above 60 meets the severe bands for primary mitral regurgitation. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on mitral regurgitation severity.

items.q: EROA is 0.15 sq cm with regurgitant volume 20 ml for mitral regurgitation. What grade is this?
items.exp: Orifice below 0.20 with volume below 30 sits in the mild band with little chamber load. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on mitral regurgitation severity.

items.q: Which extra finding confirms severe chronic mitral regurgitation?
o: Systolic flow reversal in the pulmonary veins
items.exp: A large regurgitant wave reverses vein flow in systole, which marks severe disease with atrial overload. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on supporting signs.

items.q: EROA is 0.35 sq cm with regurgitant volume 70 ml for aortic regurgitation. What grade is this?
items.exp: Orifice at or above 0.30 with volume at or above 60 meets the severe bands for aortic regurgitation. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on aortic regurgitation severity.

items.q: Vena contracta is 7 mm in aortic regurgitation. How is it graded?
o: Severe, at or above the 6 mm band
items.exp: The narrow neck above 6 mm marks a large orifice, so 7 mm reads severe rather than mild. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on vena contracta.

items.q: Pressure half time below 200 ms in acute aortic regurgitation means what?
o: Severe leak with rapid pressure equalisation
items.exp: A steep jet slope with short half time shows aortic and ventricular pressures meeting fast, which fits a large acute leak. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on pressure half time.

items.q: Holodiastolic flow reversal in the descending aorta means what in aortic regurgitation?
o: Severe leak with runoff through diastole
items.exp: Backward flow through the whole of diastole shows a large runoff volume, which marks severe regurgitation. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on descending aorta flow.

items.q: EROA is 0.50 sq cm with vena contracta 8 mm for tricuspid regurgitation. What grade is this?
items.exp: Orifice at or above 0.40 with neck at or above 7 mm meets the severe bands for tricuspid disease. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on tricuspid regurgitation severity.

items.q: Which continuous wave shape fits severe tricuspid regurgitation?
o: Dense triangular jet with early peaking
items.exp: Equalised pressures blunt the late gradient, so the jet looks dense and triangular with an early peak. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on spectral signs.

items.q: Inferior vena cava is 24 mm with minimal collapse. What right atrial pressure is reported?
items.exp: A large vein without collapse marks high atrial pressure, so around 15 mmHg is reported with the range stated. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on right atrial pressure estimation.

items.q: Inferior vena cava is 15 mm with more than half collapse. What right atrial pressure is reported?
items.exp: A small vein that collapses well marks low pressure, so the 0 to 5 band centred near 3 is reported. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on right atrial pressure estimation.

items.q: Wall thickness of 16 mm at the septum in an adult points to what?
items.exp: Thickness at or above 15 mm exceeds athlete and hypertension bands, so sarcomeric disease must be assessed. Guideline: ESC valvular and cardiomyopathy guidance cited in the ASE framework, section on hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

items.q: Ejection fraction is 25 percent with a dilated thin walled ventricle. What pattern is this?
items.exp: A large cavity with poor squeeze and thin walls marks dilated disease rather than trained or normal function. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on chamber size and function.

items.q: Right ventricular basal diameter is 48 mm. How is the chamber graded?
items.exp: The basal width above the normal band marks enlargement, which then seeks a volume or pressure cause. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on right ventricular size.

items.q: Which set of views completes the BSE minimum dataset for chamber size?
o: Parasternal, apical, subcostal and suprasternal cuts in order
items.exp: The dataset orders cuts across all windows so no chamber is missed and studies compare across labs. Guideline: BSE minimum dataset, section on minimum dataset order.

items.q: Aortic root is 45 mm in a tall young patient with a murmur. What is the concern?
o: Root dilatation needing dissection and valve assessment
items.exp: A wide root in a tall young patient raises connective tissue disease with dissection risk, so the valve and aorta need full study. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on aortic root measurement.

items.q: Stroke volume is 70 ml with heart rate 70 per minute. What is the cardiac output?
items.exp: Output equals volume per beat times beats per minute, so 70 times 70 gives 4900 ml per minute. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on cardiac output by Doppler.

items.q: Left ventricular internal diameter in diastole is markedly increased with thin walls. What does it suggest?
o: Chronic volume load with eccentric remodelling
items.exp: A wide cavity with thin walls marks volume driven remodelling rather than pressure driven thickening. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on remodelling patterns.
